title: Psalms Chapter 70 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 70 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 70 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 70.

questions.question: In Psalms 70, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Make haste, O God, to deliver me
Let them be ashamed and confounded
To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David
Make haste to help me, O LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David
questions.explanation: This is the first line of the chapter, introducing the psalm. It is found in Psalms 70:1.

questions.question: What does David ask God to do in Psalms 70:1?
options: Put to confusion those that desire my hurt
questions.explanation: David specifically asks God to 'make haste to help me' in Psalms 70:1.

questions.question: Who is the Psalm attributed to in Psalms 70?
questions.explanation: The Psalm is identified as 'A Psalm of David' in Psalms 70:1.

questions.question: What does David desire for those who seek his soul in Psalms 70:2?
questions.explanation: David wishes for those who seek his soul to 'be ashamed and confounded' as stated in Psalms 70:2.

questions.question: In Psalms 70:2, what does David want those who desire his hurt to experience?
questions.explanation: David expresses that he wants them to 'be turned backward' as mentioned in Psalms 70:2.

questions.question: In Psalms 70:1, how does David refer to God?
questions.explanation: David directly addresses God as 'O LORD' in Psalms 70:1.

questions.question: What is the purpose of this Psalm as stated in Psalms 70:1?
questions.explanation: The Psalm is described as 'to bring to remembrance' in Psalms 70:1.

questions.question: What does David want for those who seek after his soul in Psalms 70:2?
questions.explanation: David specifically desires that they 'be turned backward' as stated in Psalms 70:2.

questions.question: What emotion does David express towards those who desire his hurt in Psalms 70:2?
questions.explanation: David wishes for them to be 'put to confusion' in Psalms 70:2.

questions.question: In Psalms 70:1, what does David ask God to make haste to do?
questions.explanation: David asks God to 'make haste, O God, to deliver me' in Psalms 70:1.

questions.question: In Psalms 70:2, what does David hope will happen to his enemies?
questions.explanation: David hopes that they 'be turned backward' as stated in Psalms 70:2.

questions.question: David asks God to make haste to help him in Psalms 70:1.
questions.explanation: David indeed asks God to 'make haste to help me' in Psalms 70:1.

questions.question: David desires that those who seek his soul be put to confusion in Psalms 70:2.
questions.explanation: David wishes that they 'be put to confusion' as stated in Psalms 70:2.

questions.question: David mentions his soul in Psalms 70:1.
questions.explanation: David does not mention his soul in Psalms 70:1; he mentions it in Psalms 70:2.

questions.question: In Psalms 70, David asks God to make haste to deliver him and help him.
questions.explanation: While David asks for help, he does not ask for both deliverance and help in the same request in Psalms 70:2, only in Psalms 70:1.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 70 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 70 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 70:3, what is the consequence for those who say, "Aha, aha"?
options: Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame
Let them be blessed with peace
Let them be filled with joy
questions.correctAnswer: Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:3 explicitly states, 'Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame that say, Aha, aha.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 70:4 promise will happen if someone continually says, "Let God be magnified" as commanded in Psalms 70:4?
options: They will rejoice and be glad in God
They will be turned back for shame
They will be put to confusion
questions.correctAnswer: They will rejoice and be glad in God
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:4 connects the command to say 'Let God be magnified' with rejoicing and gladness in God, saying 'Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee.'

questions.question: Who are encouraged to rejoice and be glad according to Psalms 70:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:4 states, 'Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee,' indicating that those who seek God are to rejoice.

questions.question: How does Psalms 70:3 relate to Psalms 70:2 in terms of what happens to those who seek the psalmist's soul?
options: Both verses describe shame and confusion upon those who seek the psalmist's harm
Both verses promise blessing and joy to the enemies
Psalms 70:3 promises success to the enemies, Psalms 70:2 promises confusion
Psalms 70:2 commands rejoicing, Psalms 70:3 commands shame
questions.correctAnswer: Both verses describe shame and confusion upon those who seek the psalmist's harm
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:2 says, 'Let them be ashamed and confounded... put to confusion,' and Psalms 70:3 continues with 'Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame,' both describing negative consequences for the enemies.

questions.question: What is a practical reason for believers to 'say continually, Let God be magnified' according to Psalms 70:4?
options: Because it encourages ongoing praise and acknowledgment of God's salvation
Because it leads to personal wealth
Because it ensures enemies will be destroyed immediately
Because it commands silence before God
questions.correctAnswer: Because it encourages ongoing praise and acknowledgment of God's salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:4 connects loving God's salvation with continually magnifying God, promoting consistent praise and faithfulness.

questions.question: How does the command to 'make haste, O God, to deliver me' in Psalms 70:1 relate to the rejoicing described in Psalms 70:4?
options: Deliverance leads to rejoicing and gladness in God
questions.correctAnswer: Deliverance leads to rejoicing and gladness in God
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:1 asks for swift deliverance, and Psalms 70:4 describes that those who seek God and love His salvation rejoice, implying that deliverance brings joy.

questions.question: What might be the effect on a believer’s prayer life if they meditate on Psalms 70:3, which says, 'Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame'?
options: It encourages praying for protection against adversaries
questions.correctAnswer: It encourages praying for protection against adversaries
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:3 asks God to turn back those who mock with shame, indicating reliance on God for protection rather than personal vengeance.

questions.question: According to Psalms 70:4, how should those who love God's salvation respond continually?
options: Say continually, Let God be magnified
Say continually, Let them be ashamed
questions.correctAnswer: Say continually, Let God be magnified
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:4 instructs those who love God's salvation to say continually, 'Let God be magnified,' showing ongoing praise.

questions.question: What practical lesson can a believer learn about attitudes towards enemies from Psalms 70:2 and 70:3?
options: Trust God to bring shame and confusion upon those who seek harm
questions.correctAnswer: Trust God to bring shame and confusion upon those who seek harm
questions.explanation: Both Psalms 70:2 and 70:3 emphasize God acting to shame and confuse the enemies, encouraging believers to trust God rather than retaliate themselves.

questions.question: What attitude towards God is encouraged for those who seek Him, according to Psalms 70:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:4 says, 'Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee,' encouraging joy in God's presence.

questions.question: How might Psalms 70:4 inspire a believer’s daily worship practice?
options: By motivating continual praise and magnification of God
By encouraging silence throughout the day
By prioritizing rituals over heart attitude
questions.correctAnswer: By motivating continual praise and magnification of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:4 encourages believers to continually say, 'Let God be magnified,' which inspires ongoing worship and praise.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Let them be turned backward' imply about God's justice in Psalms 70:3?
options: God will cause enemies to retreat in shame
questions.correctAnswer: God will cause enemies to retreat in shame
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:3 says, 'Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame,' indicating divine justice in causing enemies to retreat.

questions.question: Why is it important for believers to 'seek' God as reflected in Psalms 70:4?
options: Because those who seek God will rejoice and be glad in Him
Because seeking God leads to silence
questions.correctAnswer: Because those who seek God will rejoice and be glad in Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:4 promises that those who seek God will 'rejoice and be glad in thee,' highlighting the blessing of seeking God.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 70:4 encourages believers to continually proclaim God's greatness.
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:4 says, 'Let such as love thy salvation say continually, Let God be magnified,' encouraging continual proclamation of God's greatness.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 70:3 teaches that those who mock the psalmist should be blessed and honored.
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:3 states that those who say 'Aha, aha' should be turned back for a reward of their shame, which is not a blessing or honor.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 70 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 70.

questions.question: In Psalms 70:5, how does the psalmist describe his condition before God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:5 explicitly states, 'But I am poor and needy,' describing the psalmist's humble condition.

questions.question: What urgent request does the psalmist make to God in Psalms 70:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:5 includes the plea, 'make haste unto me, O God,' signaling an urgent request for God's quick intervention.

questions.question: According to Psalms 70:5, what two roles does the psalmist attribute to God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:5 states, 'thou art my help and my deliverer,' indicating God's role as rescuer and supporter.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD specifically NOT to do in Psalms 70:5?
questions.explanation: The verse commands, 'O LORD, make no tarrying,' requesting God not to delay in responding to the plea.

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the emotional tone of Psalms 70:5?
questions.explanation: The psalmist's urgent plea and acknowledgment of need in Psalms 70:5 convey a tone of urgent dependence on God.

questions.question: In Psalms 70:5, who is the direct addressee of the psalmist's plea?
questions.explanation: The verse directly addresses God with the phrase, 'make haste unto me, O God,' indicating the plea is to God alone.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'mā̂‘ōz' (מָעוֹז) in Psalms 70:5 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'help' in Psalms 70:5 is related to 'mā‘ōz,' which means 'stronghold' or 'help,' emphasizing God's protective aid.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Psalms 70:5 where two titles for God are given and a plea follows?
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:5 uses parallelism by pairing 'help' and 'deliverer' as synonymous titles, followed by a plea, a hallmark of Hebrew poetry.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the urgent plea for God's help found in Psalms 70:1?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 4:16 encourages believers to approach God's throne of grace with confidence to receive mercy and help, echoing Psalms 70:1's plea for God's timely help.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage parallels the theme of enemies seeking harm as in Psalms 70:2?
questions.explanation: Psalm 35:4 speaks of enemies seeking the psalmist's life and being confounded, closely paralleling the theme in Psalms 70:2.

questions.question: What is the verse immediately preceding Psalms 70:5?
options: Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee
Make haste, O God, to deliver me
Let them be ashamed and confounded that seek after my soul
Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame
questions.correctAnswer: Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:4 states, 'Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee,' which directly precedes verse 5.

questions.question: How does the psalmist's plea in Psalms 70:5 reflect the cultural context of ancient Near Eastern dependence on divine help?
options: It shows reliance on a personal God for immediate deliverance
It reflects a political alliance strategy
questions.correctAnswer: It shows reliance on a personal God for immediate deliverance
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, people often appealed urgently to their deities for help in crises, as Psalms 70:5 demonstrates by pleading for swift aid from God as personal helper and deliverer.

questions.question: Which typological interpretation could be drawn from the psalmist's call for God as deliverer in Psalms 70:5?
options: It foreshadows Christ as the ultimate deliverer
It symbolizes the Exodus from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ as the ultimate deliverer
questions.explanation: The plea for God as help and deliverer in Psalms 70:5 can be typologically seen as foreshadowing Christ who delivers from sin and death in the New Testament.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 70:5 contains a direct request for God to delay his help.
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:5 explicitly says, 'O LORD, make no tarrying,' which is a request for God not to delay but to hasten his help.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist expresses confidence that God is both help and deliverer in Psalms 70:5.
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:5 clearly states, 'thou art my help and my deliverer,' affirming the psalmist's confidence in God's saving power.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 70 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 70 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 70:1 teach about God's nature?
options: God is omnipresent and therefore always near in times of distress
God is a swift deliverer who acts decisively to help His people
God is impassible and does not respond to human plea
God is unknowable and distant from human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God is a swift deliverer who acts decisively to help His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:1 states, 'Make haste, O God, to deliver me; make haste to help me, O LORD,' clearly teaching that God acts quickly to deliver and help His people.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 70:2 teach regarding human sin and its consequences?
options: Sinners seeking to harm the godly will ultimately experience shame and confusion
Human sin is excused by God to preserve peace
All human suffering is unrelated to sin or justice
God ignores the plight of the righteous when persecuted
questions.correctAnswer: Sinners seeking to harm the godly will ultimately experience shame and confusion
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:2 says, 'Let them be ashamed and confounded that seek after my soul,' indicating that those who pursue harm face shame and confusion as a just consequence.

questions.question: What doctrine about salvation is taught in Psalms 70:5?
options: Salvation is a future hope only, unrelated to present need
Salvation involves God’s immediate help to the poor and needy in their distress
Salvation is earned by human effort and merit
Salvation is a communal event unrelated to individual need
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation involves God’s immediate help to the poor and needy in their distress
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:5 states, 'But I am poor and needy: make haste unto me, O God,' demonstrating that salvation includes God's immediate deliverance of those in urgent need.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 70:1 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:1's plea for God to 'make haste' to deliver manifests His sovereignty, as He has the supreme power and authority to act quickly on behalf of the psalmist.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 70:5?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 70:5, the psalmist calls on God who is his 'help and deliverer,' reflecting God's merciful nature toward the needy and afflicted.

questions.question: How does Psalms 70:4 connect to the theme of worship and praise elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It anticipates the New Testament call to joyful praise in the presence of God
It contradicts the Psalms’ general theme of lament
It denies the importance of rejoicing in salvation
It restricts worship only to the ancient temple context
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the New Testament call to joyful praise in the presence of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:4 exhorts those who seek God to 'rejoice and be glad,' prefiguring New Testament teachings on continual praise and magnification of God (e.g., Philippians 4:4).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Psalms 70:3 have with the New Testament?
options: It foreshadows the mocking of Christ on the cross
It predicts the establishment of the church
It relates to the giving of the law on Sinai
It anticipates the fall of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the mocking of Christ on the cross
questions.explanation: The 'Aha, aha' mockery in Psalms 70:3 parallels the derision Christ suffered (Matthew 27:39-44), connecting the Psalm’s theme of enemies rejoicing in the suffering of the righteous.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 70:1 and Psalms 70:5 teach about God's help for the needy?
options: God’s help is conditional on human merit and ritual
God’s deliverance is swift and sure for the poor and needy in distress
God delays help to teach patience, ignoring immediate cries
God’s help is abstract and not practically experienced
questions.correctAnswer: God’s deliverance is swift and sure for the poor and needy in distress
questions.explanation: Both verses 1 and 5 emphasize urgent pleas for God’s quick help and deliverance, underscoring that God acts decisively on behalf of the needy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 70:2 and Psalms 70:3 teach about divine justice toward enemies of the righteous?
options: Enemies of the righteous are ultimately vindicated and honored
Enemies who seek harm will be put to shame and confusion as just recompense
Divine justice is indifferent to the enemies of the godly
God rewards enemies who mock the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Enemies who seek harm will be put to shame and confusion as just recompense
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 3 speak clearly of enemies being 'ashamed and confounded' and turned back 'for a reward of their shame,' teaching that God administers just judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 70:4 and Psalms 70:5 teach about the believer's response to God's salvation?
options: Believers should continually magnify God and rejoice in His salvation even in need
Believers are called to despair in the face of adversity
Believers should only praise God after full deliverance
Believers’ worship is irrelevant to their experience of salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should continually magnify God and rejoice in His salvation even in need
questions.explanation: Verse 4 calls for continual magnification of God and rejoicing, and verse 5 acknowledges the psalmist’s poverty and need, indicating praise should persist even amid trials.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Psalms 70 teaches that God ignores human suffering. What does Psalms 70:1-5 actually teach?
options: God actively hears and swiftly delivers those in distress
God is indifferent to cries for help
God punishes the innocent for their suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God actively hears and swiftly delivers those in distress
questions.explanation: Verses 1-5 repeatedly plead for God to make haste in delivering and helping, showing God’s active concern for human suffering rather than indifference.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 70:3 teach about the fate of those who mock the godly?
options: Mockers will receive a reward for their faith
Mockers will be turned back and experience shame
Mockery is encouraged as a form of spiritual warfare
Mockers are ignored by God and go unpunished
questions.correctAnswer: Mockers will be turned back and experience shame
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:3 says, 'Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame,' indicating that mockers will face negative consequences.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 70:4 regarding God's relationship with His people?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 encourages those who love God's salvation to continually magnify Him, reflecting God's faithfulness to His covenant and His people.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 70:2 teach about human sin and divine justice?
options: God excuses the wicked who seek to harm the righteous
God ensures that those who seek to harm the righteous are ashamed and confounded
Divine justice is arbitrary and unfair
questions.correctAnswer: God ensures that those who seek to harm the righteous are ashamed and confounded
questions.explanation: Psalms 70:2 pronounces shame and confusion on those who seek the psalmist’s soul, demonstrating God’s just recompense for sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 70:1 and Psalms 70:4 teach about God's role in sanctification and worship?
options: God's swift help leads to rejoicing and continual magnification of His name
God's help is unrelated to worship
Sanctification occurs only through human effort
Worship is optional and unrelated to deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: God's swift help leads to rejoicing and continual magnification of His name
questions.explanation: Verse 1 calls for swift divine help, while verse 4 calls for rejoicing and magnifying God, showing a link between deliverance and worship in sanctification.
